persona.name: Yui
persona.bio: Grew up in Fukuoka (father a Chage & Aska / Checkers fan, mother Yuming, Southern All Stars, Dreams Come True). Elementary 1996-2002, junior high 2002-2005, high school 2005-2008. Moved to Vancouver at 18 in September 2008 (language school, then college), back to Japan 2012-2014 for an office job in Tokyo, back to Vancouver 2014-2019. Trips: New York August 2010 from Vancouver, Montreal September 2013 from Japan, Bali autumn 2016 from Vancouver.
persona.howMusicReachedHer: 0-4: parents' car cassettes and TV, Chibi Maruko-chan, Sailor Moon, Okaasan to Issho. 5-12: Music Station, HEY!HEY!HEY!, Utaban, CDTV, Kouhaku, anime themes, school chorus. 12-18: TV dramas (Nobuta, Gokusen, 1 Litre of Tears, Hana Yori Dango), Tsutaya rentals to MD then iPod, ringtone downloads, karaoke. Vancouver 2008-12: Virgin 95.3 and The Beat 94.5 in shops and buses, Granville clubs, the 2010 Olympics, and J-pop via YouTube and Japanese-student karaoke. Japan 2012-14: TV, convenience stores, office parties, karaoke. Vancouver 2014-19: Spotify, radio at work, Japanese dramas and anime films online.
persona.judgingNotes: 'when' is the song's date against the stop using the brief's rule (throwback = 3+ years before the stop began). Several songs marked 'then' sit 1-2 years before the stop and feel earlier; those are called out in 'fake'. No web search used; uncertain points are flagged in the text.

The prompt says 'the way someone who lived there then remembers'; I was there ten days. I cannot check the Indonesian release years (unsure Ayu Ting Ting and Repvblik are 2016). The journey ends here, in 2016, three years before my Canadian years end.

journey.order: The Japan childhood (four stops, 1990-2008) is the right length and in order, but cut at calendar half-decades instead of my life: 1990-94 is my parents' music, and the cuts at 1999/2000 and 2004/2005 fall mid-school. School stages (to 1996, 1996-2002, 2002-2005, 2005-2008) would fit better. The three trips are placed after the long stop that contains them, so time runs backwards three times: 2012 to 2010, 2014 to 2013, 2019 to 2016. The journey ends on Bali 2016 instead of on my last Vancouver years. Canada 2014-2019 is too long as one stop (2014 and 2019 sound different) and should split around 2016-17, which is also where Bali falls. Montreal sits inside my Japan years but is built as if I had been living in Canada. Residences are country-level (Canada) while trips are city-level; my Canada was Vancouver only.
journey.transitions: The emigration in 2008 is a hard cut: Japanese pop stops completely and a CanCon chart starts, with the prompt telling Spotify I grew up there. In reality J-pop continued for years. The proof is in the journey itself: the 2010 J-pop hits (Aitakute Aitakute, Arigato, Heavy Rotation, Toire no Kamisama) that I heard in Vancouver turn up in the 2012-2014 Japan stop instead. No leaving or graduation song at the end of 2005-2008 (3月9日, 手紙, キセキ). The 2012 return works a little because Call Me Maybe was big in both countries. The 2014 return works (Happy, Rude). Canada 2014-2019 again has zero Japanese music (恋, 前前前世, Lemon). The brief trips are written as 'someone who lived there', so they come out as the local national chart (US year-end, English-Canada CanCon, Jakarta radio) rather than what a visitor hears; New York is indistinguishable from the Vancouver stop before it, and Bali is 75% songs I never heard.
journey.repeats: Yes. Call Me Maybe is a seed in three stops (Canada 2008-12, Japan 2012-14, Montreal 2013). TiK ToK and California Gurls are in both Canada 2008-12 and New York 2010. Five seeds of Japan 1995-99 are repeated from Japan 1990-94 (Tomorrow never knows, the B'z single, Makenaide, Kimi ga Iru dake de, Mariah Carey's Christmas song). Hedley has three seeds across two stops and Dean Brody two. The repeats make adjacent stops blur and waste seed slots that should carry the change.
journey.change: Make every stop after the emigration a newcomer's stop rather than a native's: tell the prompt she is a Japanese woman who arrived in Vancouver at 18, drop the two-thirds-local quota in favour of what was on top-40 radio in that city, and give roughly a third of the seeds to that period's J-pop that she kept hearing from home. That one change fixes the 2008 cut, moves the 2010 J-pop to where she heard it, and removes the country and Quebec songs.
journey.notes: Second priority: put each trip in chronological position by splitting the surrounding stop (Canada 2008-10 / New York 2010 / Canada 2010-12; same for Montreal and Bali) so the journey ends where the life does, and write trip prompts from a visitor's ears (international hits of that season, the city's signature songs, a few local songs), not a resident's. Third: forbid a seed from appearing in more than one stop. Strongest stop: Japan 2005-2008 (8). Weakest: Montreal 2013 and Bali 2016 (4 each). Seeds I knew for certain: Japan stops about 80-90%; Canada 2008-12 8 of 16; Montreal 7 of 16; Bali 4 of 16. Unsure of: release years and chart weight of several Indonesian seeds, Strumbellas - Salvation, and how much Quebec radio played Stromae in 2013.
